instructions: Install the optional planner definition. Supply the named research files as text with stable, anonymized session/case IDs.
This read-only job analyzes existing evidence and code. It does not recruit participants, collect analytics, operate a browser, or establish that a design is usable.

tasks.task: Analyze research/onboarding/interviews.md for observed onboarding failures and successful strategies. Extract evidence by session ID and source location.
acceptance: Separate what participants said or did from interpretations and proposed solutions.
Retain contradictory cases; do not invent participants, quotes, or prevalence estimates.

tasks.task: Analyze research/onboarding/support.md for recurring onboarding issues, workarounds, and affected journey stages.
acceptance: Cite case IDs and source locations; distinguish duplicate tickets from independent reports.
Explain sampling limits rather than equating ticket counts with population frequency.

tasks.task: Inspect src/onboarding and research/onboarding/usability-notes.md. Map the intended journey, validation errors, empty states, and recovery routes. Contrast the implementation with recorded observations.
acceptance: Cite code and notes for each friction point.
Label source-based usability hypotheses separately from actual observed user behavior.

tasks.task: Group the interview, support, and journey evidence into findings. Propose changes for the most consequential onboarding failures and identify what should be tested with users next.
acceptance: Each finding links observations, interpretation, affected journey stage, proposed change, and confidence.
Include counterevidence and explain prioritization by user impact and evidence strength.

tasks.task: Audit the synthesis against the original local evidence. Look for unsupported causal claims, lost minority experiences, fabricated quotes, and solutions that do not address the observed problem.
acceptance: Cite source locations for corrections and counterexamples.
Return unresolved research questions even when the synthesis seems plausible.

tasks.task: Turn the evidence and challenge into an ordered UX improvement backlog and a plan for the next usability session. Preserve traceability to the source observations.
acceptance: For each item provide a user outcome, bounded implementation scope, and observable acceptance criteria.
Define participant tasks and success signals for real usability evaluation; do not claim an agent simulated a user study.
Separate implementation-ready items from questions needing further research. Return the backlog in the task result.
